limitations: No .jcodemunch.jsonc architecture.layers rules are defined, so get_layer_violations returned an empty result rather than a real check; layering was instead assessed by direct read of electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts, api/index.ts, server/src/*, src/lib/*.

Runtime behavior (which backend, server/ or api/, actually serves a given deployment) was inferred from vercel.json rewrites, package.json scripts, and src/lib/auth-client.ts defaults, not from an executed deployment.
Coverage is limited to the 57 files jCodeMunch indexed (src/, electron/, server/, api/, scripts/, root config); generated/build output directories were not inspected.

findings.title: Two independently-maintained backend implementations (server/ Hono app, api/index.ts Vercel handler) duplicate DB schema and Better Auth setup and have already drifted

identity.assertion: api/index.ts re-declares the Postgres schema (user/session/account/verification/projects) and the betterAuth() config inline instead of importing server/src/db/schema.ts and server/src/auth.ts, and its copy of the projects table has already diverged from the server/ copy (missing the clientProfileId column and the entire client_profiles table); its raw-Node handler also only serves /api/health and /api/auth/**, not the /api/projects CRUD routes that server/src/index.ts implements for the same responsibility.

evidence.detail: const projects = pgTable('projects', {...}) — a second, hand-copied definition of the same 'projects' table declared in server/src/db/schema.ts (line 70), missing the clientProfileId column and the client_profiles table entirely.

clientProfiles/projects tables (with clientProfileId FK) are the canonical schema used by server/src/db/index.ts and server/src/auth.ts; api/index.ts has no import of this file and no reference to it.

const auth = betterAuth({...}) duplicates server/src/auth.ts's betterAuth() call (same options shape, same fallback secret string 'marlex-content-engine-super-secret-key-2026') as an independent inline config rather than a shared import.

handler() only routes '/api/health' and '/api/auth/**' to 404 for everything else — it does not implement the '/api/projects' GET/POST routes that server/src/index.ts (lines 34-65) exposes for the same 'projects' resource.
rewrites '/api/(.*)' -> '/api' confirms api/index.ts is the actual serverless entry point used in the Vercel deployment (the production backend).

sanitizeBaseUrl() falls back to 'https://marlex.vercel.app' for Electron/production, i.e. api/index.ts (not server/src/index.ts) is the backend real clients talk to in production and in the desktop app.
"server:dev": "tsx server/src/index.ts" is the only script that runs server/src/index.ts; it is a separate, locally-run entry point never wired into the Vercel build or imported by api/index.ts.

verification.note: Independent verifier confirmed via vercel.json, api/index.ts, and server/src/index.ts: api/index.ts is the sole Vercel production entry and does not implement /api/projects; server/src/index.ts (which does) never runs in that deployment (`if (!process.env.VERCEL)` guard, only started by the local-only `server:dev` script). jCodeMunch find_importers/find_references on server/src/index.ts both return zero hits; repo-wide grep finds only the package.json script reference. No alternate deploy path found.

findings.title: generateContentPackage() in src/lib/ai/llm-client.ts mixes four unrelated AI-integration responsibilities in one 150-line function

identity.assertion: generateContentPackage (lines 316-465) is a single function that branches over 5 mutually exclusive execution modes — Electron-only local-CLI invocation via window.electronAPI.executeCLI, and three separate hand-rolled fetch() integrations against OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini's REST APIs — plus JSON-cleanup/parsing and a synthetic fallback-generation path, with no shared provider abstraction; jCodeMunch's hotspot scan measures this as the highest-complexity function in the repo (cyclomatic 41, max_nesting 10).

evidence.detail: config.mode === 'local_cli' branch calls window.electronAPI.executeCLI, an Electron-only IPC bridge, directly from what src/lib/ presents as shared/platform-neutral runtime code.
config.provider === 'openai' branch does its own fetch() to api.openai.com with bespoke request/response shaping.
config.provider === 'anthropic' branch does a second, independently-shaped fetch() to api.anthropic.com, including a 'dangerously-allow-browser' header, again with no shared HTTP helper.
config.provider === 'gemini' branch does a third independently-shaped fetch() to generativelanguage.googleapis.com.

After all four branches, the same function also owns brace-matched JSON extraction, JSON.parse with try/catch, and construction of the final GenerationResult, plus a synthetic buildDynamicFallback() call on parse failure — none of which is provider-specific.
